title: MY Scoring Cohort — Behaviorally Anchored Rating Scale (BARS)
description: Five-point rubric for rating candidate fit in the Malaysia (MY) cohort. Each dimension has behavioral anchors at every level (1-5). Rate every dimension before forming an overall rating. See rater-kit.md for Frame-of-Reference calibration.

dimensions.name: Hard Skills & Technical Competency Fit
dimensions.description: Match between the candidate's demonstrated technical skills and the tools, processes, and systems used in the target role.

anchors.1: Skills are unrelated or absent for the target role; no evidence of any required tool, process, or system; cannot perform core tasks without extensive training.
anchors.2: Some adjacent skills are present but key required tools are missing or used only at a basic level; performance would require significant ramp-up and rework risk is high.
anchors.3: Required core skills are present with 1-3 years of applied use; can perform the role's standard tasks independently with normal supervision.
anchors.4: Core skills are mastered and adjacent or advanced tools are also in use; skills are recent, sustained across multiple projects, and the candidate can train others.
anchors.5: Recognized expert: breadth and depth exceed the role; skills are current and directly transferable; demonstrably raises the capability of the whole team.

dimensions.name: Experience Depth & Domain Relevance
dimensions.description: Depth and relevance of the work history relative to the role's core responsibilities.

anchors.1: No relevant work experience; roles are unrelated and the candidate cannot point to a single comparable responsibility.
anchors.2: 1-2 years of partially relevant experience; responsibilities overlap only at the edges and most duties would be new to the candidate.
anchors.3: 3-5 years of relevant experience; the candidate has owned the core responsibilities end-to-end in a comparable setting.
anchors.4: 5-8 years of relevant experience with increasing scope; the candidate has led projects or initiatives in the domain with quantifiable outcomes.
anchors.5: 8+ years of deep, directly relevant experience including complex, high-stakes work; the candidate is recognized within the industry.

dimensions.name: Domain Context
dimensions.description: Familiarity with the operating context: Precision Engineering, FMCG, B2B SaaS, Bayan Lepas Free Industrial Zone, or Klang Valley.

anchors.1: No exposure to any listed context; cannot articulate how the industry works or what its constraints are.
anchors.2: Peripheral exposure only (e.g., supplier side or an adjacent industry); understands the surface but not the operational realities.
anchors.3: Worked within at least one relevant context; understands key constraints such as quality standards, margins, lead times, and compliance, and can apply them.
anchors.4: Worked in multiple relevant contexts including a priority one such as the Penang FIZ or Klang Valley; speaks the language of the industry fluently.
anchors.5: Deep multi-context expertise; has navigated industry-specific crises or transformations; carries network and references inside the priority context.

dimensions.name: Career Progression & Stability
dimensions.description: Tenure, promotion trajectory, employment gaps, and job-hopping signals across the career history.

anchors.1: Pattern of short tenures under six months with no progression; unexplained gaps; repeated departures without advancement.
anchors.2: Mixed pattern: some short stints or a gap of six or more months that is unexplained; progression is flat or unclear.
anchors.3: Stable tenure of two or more years per role on average with at least one clear promotion or scope increase.
anchors.4: Sustained growth: increasing responsibility across roles, two or more promotions or step changes, and no unexplained gaps.
anchors.5: Long-term commitment with repeated advancement and internal mobility; the trajectory is monotonic, verifiable, and free of unexplained interruptions.

dimensions.name: Education, Certifications & Credentials
dimensions.description: Formal qualifications and credentials relevant to the role, plus bilingual working fluency in English and Bahasa Malaysia.

anchors.1: No relevant qualification or credential; fluency in neither English nor Bahasa Malaysia is sufficient for the workplace.
anchors.2: Basic qualification (e.g., SPM/STPM) with limited relevance, or a relevant certificate with no evidence of applied use; weak in one working language.
anchors.3: Relevant diploma or degree (e.g., UTM, TAR UMT) or a recognized certification (PMP, CIDB, ACCA) with evidence of use; bilingual working fluency.
anchors.4: Strong qualification plus one or two advanced or directly role-mapped certifications; full professional fluency in both English and Bahasa Malaysia.
anchors.5: Highest-tier credentials such as professional registration, advanced degrees, or multiple in-domain certifications with recognized standing; fully bilingual and able to negotiate and draft in both languages.
